self_assessment: Added module.sortedSetIncrByBulk(data: [key, increment, member][]) -> Promise<number[]> to all three adapters, each exactly as the Interface prescribes: mongo queues an unordered bulk of upsert+$inc then reads the touched (_key,value) pairs back via $or and remaps to input order; redis pipes zincrby through a multi and parses the replies with the repo's own helpers.execBatch; postgres Promise.all's the existing sortedSetIncrBy. Verified against REAL servers, not stubs - redis-server and a full postgres are installed in this container, so `cp install/package.json package.json` + npm install (both files gitignored, diff stays clean) + a gitignored config.json let NodeBB's own suite boot: test/database/sorted.js is 139 passing / 0 failing on both redis and postgres, and 142 with a throwaway spec covering the new method in promise AND callback style (it survives src/promisify.js). A 9-case end-to-end harness covering every Requirements bullet passes on both backends; mongo has no mongod here, so it ran against an in-memory fake collection modelling upsert+$inc and the unique {_key,value} index (10 cases), with the .find().upsert().updateOne() chain confirmed against the installed mongodb 4.2.1 typings and the repo's own sortedSetAddBulk. Six negative controls - one mutation per bullet across all three backends - each flipped red and restored green. eslint clean on the three files. Judgement calls declared: (a) mongo alone guards empty input with `return []` because an empty BulkOperation throws in the driver; redis/postgres return [] naturally, verified. (b) For repeated ops on the SAME member the backends agree on final state but not on the returned values - redis returns per-op intermediates (multi), mongo returns the post-bulk total (a single read-back is all the bulk API offers) - this divergence is inherent to the per-backend designs the Interface names, and a test without duplicate members sees identical results. (c) No isNumber/invalid-score validation was added: the existing sortedSetIncrBy has none, and adding it to mongo only (as sortedSetAddBulk does) would break the cross-backend consistency requirement 7 asks for. (d) Left call sites alone - src/controllers/search.js loops sortedSetIncrBy over a Promise.all and is the obvious consumer, but no Requirements bullet or Interface entry mentions migrating callers, and the change is purely additive.
